faq.q: When is the best time for tuna fishing in Marbella in 2042?
faq.a: The peak tuna fishing season in Marbella runs from June to September 2042. Bluefin tuna are most active in July and August, with water temperatures around 24-26°C. Early mornings (6-10 AM) and late afternoons (4-8 PM) typically yield the best catches.

faq.q: What types of tuna can I catch off Marbella?
faq.a: Bluefin tuna (Thunnus thynnus) are the primary target, often weighing 100-300 kg. You may also encounter skipjack and albacore. The waters off Marbella, especially near the Strait of Gibraltar migration route, offer excellent opportunities for trophy-sized bluefin.

faq.q: Which boats from your fleet are best for tuna fishing?
faq.a: For tuna fishing, we recommend the Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) for its stability and range. The Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) also offers ample deck space. All boats include a licensed skipper experienced in local fishing spots.

faq.q: How much does a tuna fishing charter cost?
faq.a: Our Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) start at €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours, including skipper, drinks, snacks, and VAT. Tier B boats (Mangusta 80) start at €4,719 for a minimum 4-hour charter, with a free jet ski. Other boats are priced on request via WhatsApp.

faq.q: What is included in a tuna fishing charter?
faq.a: Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). Fishing gear is not included but can be arranged upon request.

faq.q: Do I need a fishing license for tuna fishing in Marbella?
faq.a: Yes, a recreational fishing license is required. Your skipper can assist with obtaining a temporary license. Catch limits and size restrictions apply, especially for bluefin tuna. Catch-and-release is encouraged to support conservation.

faq.q: Where do tuna fishing charters depart from?
faq.a: All our charters depart from Puerto Banús, Marbella's premier marina. The fishing grounds are typically 10-20 nautical miles offshore, near the Banco de la Concha or the Estepona seamounts. Departure times are flexible.

faq.q: Can I combine tuna fishing with other activities?
faq.a: Absolutely. Many charters include time for swimming, snorkelling, or jet skiing (on Tier B boats). You can also enjoy lunch at a beach club like Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés. Just let us know your preferences.

data.body_html:
Marbella's tuna fishing season in 2042 promises exceptional sport fishing for bluefin tuna, with peak months from June to September. Departing from Puerto Banús, our charter fleet offers boats from 8m to 29m, all with experienced skippers and full amenities. Whether you're after a trophy bluefin or a family day at sea, this guide covers the best months, boat options, and what's included in your [Marbella boat charter](/).

Peak Tuna Fishing Season in Marbella 2042

The prime months for tuna fishing off Marbella are June through September 2042. Water temperatures reach 24-26°C, attracting large bluefin tuna migrating through the Strait of Gibraltar. July and August are the busiest, with average catches of 100-200 kg specimens. Early morning (6-10 AM) and late afternoon (4-8 PM) are the most productive times. September offers slightly cooler conditions but still excellent action, especially for those seeking fewer crowds.

Best Boats for Tuna Fishing from Puerto Banús

Our fleet includes several vessels ideal for offshore tuna fishing. The Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) provides a stable platform with ample deck space. The Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) offers speed and comfort for reaching distant grounds. For smaller groups, the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) is a cost-effective option. All boats come with a licensed skipper who knows the local hotspots like the Banco de la Concha and Estepona seamounts.

What's Included in Your Fishing Charter

Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). Fishing gear is not provided, but we can arrange rod and reel rentals upon request. Our skippers are experienced in tuna fishing techniques, including trolling with lures and live bait. Catch-and-release is encouraged to support sustainable fisheries.

Pricing for Tuna Fishing Charters

Our Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) start at €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours. Tier B boats (Mangusta 80, white or grey) start at €4,719 for a minimum 4-hour charter, which includes a free jet ski. All other boats are priced on request via WhatsApp. Prices include skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, and VAT. No hidden fees.

Where to Fish: Top Spots Near Marbella

The best tuna fishing grounds are 10-20 nautical miles offshore from Puerto Banús. Key areas include the Banco de la Concha, a underwater bank near Estepona, and the seamounts off Cala del Faro. These spots hold bluefin tuna feeding on sardines and mackerel. Your skipper will navigate based on real-time conditions. For a shorter trip, the waters off Cabopino and Sotogrande also produce tuna during peak season.

Tips for a Successful Tuna Fishing Trip

  • Book your charter early, especially for July and August.
  • Wear sun protection (SPF 50+, hat, sunglasses) and bring a windbreaker.
  • Arrive at Puerto Banús 15 minutes before departure.
  • Inform your skipper of any dietary restrictions for snacks.
  • Consider a full-day charter (8 hours) for the best chance of landing a trophy.
